source_units.text: The application separates two activities:
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - **Drawing** — editing the artwork inside a drawing cell (section 02). Drawing tools work in the Drawing view and also directly in the Camera view, where they edit the current cell of the selected element through its full scene transform.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - **Scene planning (staging)** — placing, layering and animating elements inside a 3-D scene seen through a camera.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: Both are available at all times from one command set; there is no global mode switch. The scene-planning tool set and the drawing tool set are independent: each remembers its own current tool, and selecting a scene-planning tool does not change the remembered drawing tool (and vice versa).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: The scene-planning workspace consists of the **Camera view**, **Top view**, **Side view** (§3), the Timeline (section 04), the **Properties** panel (which shows the properties of the selected node, §8, §9.4, §12.3, §13.5–13.6), and the **function editor** (§11). A default scene-planning workspace layout containing Camera view, Timeline, Side view, Top view, scene manager and Properties MUST be provided (layout design per section 01).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: The scene is a right-handed 3-D space ("scene space", also "field space"):
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | X | right | left | E / W | horizontal position |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Y | up | down | N / S | vertical position |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: Numeric fields and the function editor display distances with a direction suffix (e.g. `3.5 E`, `1.25 S`, `2 B`) when *Show Units* is on; the suffix replaces the minus sign. Agents always use signed numbers (§19.2).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: **Design decision — units.** The canonical unit of scene space is the **field**. 1 field = 1 inch = 2.54 cm, isotropic on X, Y and Z. Positions are stored in fields (double precision) and converted only for display. Display units are selectable: fields (default), inches, centimetres. Angles are stored and displayed in degrees (the function editor MAY offer radians as a display alternative). Time is measured in frames (1-based integers for keyframes; real numbers for derived times such as control-point passage times).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: **Design decision — table plane and field guide.** The plane Z = 0 is the *table plane*. Through the default camera (§2.7) the camera frame covers exactly **12 fields horizontally** on the table plane, centred on the origin; its height is 12 × (camera height ÷ camera width) fields (9 fields for 4:3, 6.75 fields for 16:9). The 12-field and 16-field guides of section 02 are drawn against this convention.
source_units.note: Round-1 divergence closed by response implementation; see round-2 finding closure table.

source_units.text: | Scene (world) space | centre of the default camera frame on the table plane | X right, Y up, Z toward camera | field | all world positions, `anim.evaluate` results |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Node-local space | the node's own origin after its local transform | as its parent, transformed | field | child placement, pivots, bone rest data |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Parent space | the parent node's local space (scene space for top-level nodes) | — | field | a node's position/rotation/scale/skew values |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Drawing space | drawing centre | X right, Y up | field | drawing content (section 02) |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Camera output (render) space | top-left of the camera frame | x right, y **down** | output pixel | rendering, `anim.projection.get`, screen bounds |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: **Design decision — drawing space mapping.** Drawing content is expressed in fields with the origin at the drawing centre and Y up. An element with an identity transform at Z = 0, seen through the default camera, displays its drawing exactly as the Drawing view shows it against the 12-field guide. If section 02 adopts a different drawing unit, a single fixed conversion factor is applied before the element transform. A bitmap image imported at native size maps one image pixel to one camera output pixel on the table plane through the default camera (i.e. 12 ÷ camera width fields per pixel).
source_units.note: Round-1 divergence closed by response implementation; see round-2 finding closure table.

source_units.text: All of the following are **transformable nodes** (also called "nodes" below). Each is an element of the scene's element tree (section 04) and owns the transformation block described in §1.5.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Drawing element (vector), image element (bitmap), media element (video), annotation element | yes | Visible content. Can be animated directly or through a parent peg. |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Peg | no | Invisible transformation carrier. Children inherit its transformation. |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Camera | no (frame drawn in views) | Point of view; the scene's *current camera* defines the Camera view and the exported image. |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Skeleton (with bone group, bones and skin group) | bones drawn in views | Bone rig that deforms the artwork placed in its skin group (§13). The skeleton node itself transforms like a peg. |
source_units.note: SI-097: skeleton transform only; bone kinematics excluded.

source_units.text: There is no limit on the number of pegs, cameras or skeletons in a scene other than available memory.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: Every transformable node has two transformation layers:
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - **Static (layout) values** — offset (X, Y, Z), rotation, scale X/Y, skew, pivots. They apply to all frames and never create keyframes. They are edited with the Select tool (§5.1), the Properties panel and `anim.transform.set` with `target: "static"`.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - **Animated values** — channels that vary over time (§1.6), edited with the keyframing tools (Transform, Rotate, Skew, Scale, Motion), keyframe commands, the function editor and motion recording.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: **Design decision — combination rule.** For a frame *f* the *effective local values* of a node are:
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | position | static offset + animated position (motion path, §9–§10.5); animated position is (0,0,0) when the node has no motion keyframe |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | rotation | static rotation + animated rotation (default 0) + orient-to-path angle (§8.3, when enabled) |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | scale X, scale Y | static scale × animated scale (default 1 each) |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | skew | static skew + animated skew (default 0), clamped to −89…+89° |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: These rules are used everywhere: in rendering, in tool feedback, in the Properties panel, in `anim.evaluate`.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: Each animatable parameter is a **channel**, a function of the node's local frame. Channel identifiers are part of the agent interface:
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `position` | peg, element, camera, skeleton | 3-D (X, Y, Z) | field | motion path: TCB spline through motion points (§9) |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `position.x`, `position.y`, `position.z` | same | 1-D projections of `position` | field | edited as projections in the function editor (§11.4) |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `velocity` | any node with a `position` channel | 1-D | field (distance travelled along the path) | timing along the path (§10.5) |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `pivot.x`, `pivot.y` | peg, element, skeleton | 1-D each (together: the *pivot path*) | field | 1-D function (§10.3) |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `rotation` | peg, element, camera (roll), skeleton, bone | 1-D | degree | 1-D function |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `scale.x`, `scale.y` | peg, element, skeleton | 1-D | factor | 1-D function |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `skew` | peg, element, skeleton | 1-D | degree | 1-D function |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `fov` | camera (when FOV mode is dynamic) | 1-D | degree | 1-D function |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `bone.x`, `bone.y` | bone (root bones only, §13.2) | 1-D | field | 1-D function |
source_units.note: SI-097: skeleton transform only; bone kinematics excluded.

source_units.text: Every channel spans the node's duration, has keyframes, and follows the node's loop setting (§8.4).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: A **motion point** is a point of a motion path. It is either
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - a **keyframe** — *locked in time*: tied to an integer frame at which the node is exactly at that point; or
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - a **control point** — *not locked in time*: shapes the path; the (possibly fractional) frame at which the node passes it is derived from the velocity channel (§10.5).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: *Lock in time* converts a control point into a keyframe (at the nearest integer frame, §9.4); unlocking converts a keyframe into a control point. A motion path always begins and ends with a keyframe (§9.6).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: Keyframes of 1-D channels (rotation, scale, skew, pivot, FOV, bone channels) are simply key points with an integer frame and a value. A node "has a keyframe at frame *f*" when any of its channels has a key at *f*; the Timeline (section 04) shows which channels are keyed at each frame (position, rotation, scale, skew, pivot, velocity, and for bones position, rotation and length), and shows on a collapsed parent that one of its descendants has a keyframe.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: The interval between two consecutive keyframes of a channel is a **segment**. A segment is either **tweened** (interpolated) or **constant** (the value of the start keyframe holds until the next keyframe, then jumps). For the `position` channel the depth (Z) component can additionally be made constant independently (*Constant Z*, §9.3). Whether new keyframes start constant segments is governed by the *Create constant keyframes* preference (§16).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: This chapter is normative. Implementations MUST produce results equal to these formulas within 1e-6 field / 1e-6 degree (before display rounding).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - Points are column vectors (x, y, z, 1)ᵀ; transforms are 4 × 4 affine matrices applied as p′ = M · p.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - Matrices are serialised row-major as 16 numbers `[m00, m01, m02, m03, m10, …, m33]` (translation in m03, m13, m23).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - Angles are degrees. **Positive rotation is counter-clockwise** as seen from the front (from +Z looking toward −Z, i.e. as seen through the default camera).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - Rotation, skew and scale act only in the X/Y plane; nodes are flat planes parallel to the table plane. Only translation changes Z.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: Elementary matrices (only the upper-left 3 × 3 and translation column shown; all others identity):
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - T(x, y, z): translation.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - R(θ): rotation in X/Y — `[[cos θ, −sin θ, 0], [sin θ, cos θ, 0], [0, 0, 1]]`.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - K(κ): horizontal skew (shear) — `[[1, tan κ, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]`, so x′ = x + y·tan κ. Positive skew leans the top of an upright shape to the right. Shear has determinant 1, so skew preserves area.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - S(sx, sy): scale — `[[sx, 0, 0], [0, sy, 0], [0, 0, 1]]`. Negative factors mirror (flips, §6.3). |sx|, |sy| MUST be ≥ 0.001; smaller magnitudes are rejected with `anim.valueOutOfRange`.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: With effective values (§1.5) — position P = (px, py, pz), rotation θ, skew κ, scale (sx, sy), rotation pivot cr and scale pivot cs (2-D points in parent space relative to the node origin, z = 0):
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: ``` M_local = T(P) · T(cr) · R(θ) · T(−cr) · T(cs) · K(κ) · S(sx, sy) · T(−cs) ```
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: i.e. scale first, then skew (both about the scale pivot), then rotation about the rotation pivot, then translation.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Element (drawing/image/media/annotation) | *rotationPivot* + animated pivot when *Use rotation pivot* is on; otherwise equal to cs | *scalePivot* + animated pivot |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | Peg, skeleton | *pivot* + animated pivot if *Apply pivot to* ∈ {rotation, both}; else (0, 0) | *pivot* + animated pivot if *Apply pivot to* ∈ {scaling, both}; else (0, 0) |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: Defaults: element pivots (0, 0) (= drawing centre); peg pivot (0, 0); *Apply pivot to* = rotation (pegs) and rotation (skeletons; skeletons offer rotation or scaling only).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: **Design decision — drawing-pivot option for pegs.** A peg MAY have *Use child drawing pivot* on. When on and the peg has exactly one drawing element as direct child, the peg's static pivot is taken as that child's static scale pivot plus the child's static X/Y offset; otherwise the option has no effect.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: ``` W(node, F) = W(parent, F) · M_local(node, f_node(F))       W(scene root) = identity ```
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: where *F* is the scene frame and f_node(F) the node's local frame (§2.10). This applies recursively through any number of pegs, effects, skeletons and elements (drawings may be parented to drawings for cut-out puppets). The parent's channels are evaluated at the same scene frame as the child.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: To report world (or combined) rotation, scale and skew, the X/Y part A = `[[a, c], [b, d]]` of a matrix is decomposed as A = R(θ) · K(κ) · S(sx, sy):
source_units.note: Round-1 divergence closed by response implementation; see round-2 finding closure table.

source_units.text: ``` sx = sqrt(a² + b²);   θ = atan2(b, a) (c′, d′) = R(−θ) · (c, d) sy = d′;   κ = atan(c′ / sy)          (sy = 0 is impossible because |scale| ≥ 0.001) ```
source_units.note: Round-1 divergence closed by response implementation; see round-2 finding closure table.

source_units.text: A mirrored matrix (determinant < 0) therefore reports a negative sy. Agents receive both the matrix and this decomposition from `anim.evaluate`.
source_units.note: Round-1 divergence closed by response implementation; see round-2 finding closure table.

source_units.text: - The camera looks along its local −Z axis with local +Y up. Its **view matrix** is the inverse of its *rigid world transform*: **Design decision** — only translation and Z rotation are taken from the camera's world matrix (position = W · (0,0,0,1); roll = θ from the decomposition of W); scale and skew inherited from ancestors are ignored.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - **FOV is the horizontal field of view** of the camera frame, in degrees, range 1…179.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - Projection of a scene point p: q = V · p (camera space). Let depth d = −q.z. Points with d ≤ 0.1 field (near plane) are not drawn; there is no far plane. With h = tan(FOV / 2), camera output size W × H pixels:
source_units.note: C32-R2-01 / SI-104: tan(FOV/2) is replaced by the exact-default tangent only for explicit 41.1121.

source_units.text: ``` xn = q.x / (d · h)                     (−1 … +1 across the frame width) yn = q.y / (d · h · H / W)             (−1 … +1 across the frame height) pixel x = (xn + 1) / 2 · W pixel y = (1 − yn) / 2 · H             (y down) ```
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - Consequently an element at depth Z (camera on the Z axis at distance D from the table plane) appears scaled by D ÷ (D − Z) relative to the table plane: F values bring it closer and enlarge it; B values shrink it.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - The camera output size and frame rate are project settings (sections 01 and 09); the camera aspect ratio = W ÷ H.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: **Design decision.** Default FOV = 2·atan(0.375) ≈ **41.1121°**; default camera static offset = **(0, 0, 16)** fields, roll 0. With these values the 12-field width of the table plane exactly fills the frame (6 ÷ tan(FOV/2) = 16). Every new scene is created with one camera named "Camera" whose parent is a peg named "Camera Peg" (identity transform), and that camera is the scene's current camera. Animating the camera is normally done on the camera peg.
source_units.note: SI-102 exact default is stored and projects to twelve fields; inherited premise corrected by ruling.

source_units.text: **Design decision:** each segment is sampled at 64 uniform parameter steps (65 points); the cumulative chord length of these samples defines arc length. To find the point at arc length s, locate the bracketing samples, interpolate the parameter linearly between them, and evaluate C exactly at that parameter. The same sampling is used for display, picking, frame markers and timing, so all clients agree. Paths are drawn as polylines of at least these samples.

source_units.text: Every 1-D channel is a list of key points `{frame, value, constantSegment, handles}`; between two keys k0 = (t0, v0) and k1 = (t1, v1) the shape depends on the channel's **curve type**:
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `spline` | Cubic Bézier in (frame, value) space with P0 = (t0, v0), P1 = (t0 + a, v0 + b) (right handle of k0), P2 = (t1 + c, v1 + d) (left handle of k1), P3 = (t1, v1). Handle frame offsets are clamped to 0 ≤ a ≤ t1 − t0 and −(t1 − t0) ≤ c ≤ 0, which keeps the curve a function of time. To evaluate frame f, solve x(u) = f for u ∈ [0, 1] (unique by monotonicity; to 1e-9) and return y(u). Handles are *smooth* (left and right handle collinear through the key; editing one rotates the other, lengths independent) or *broken* (independent); default smooth. |
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: | `interpolation` | The same Bézier, but handles are not free: each segment carries an easing preset (§10.4) that fixes P1 and P2 in normalised segment space. |

source_units.text: - The **velocity channel** V(f) is the distance travelled along the path at frame f (displayed in distance units).
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - At every motion keyframe V is **pinned**: V(fj) = Sj. Pins are implicit; they move with their keyframe and cannot be deleted or changed in value directly.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - Between pins the segment shape is a 1-D curve (spline handles or easing preset; default per §10.2). The user may add intermediate velocity key points (e.g. to pause mid-segment). **Design decision — storage:** intermediate velocity values and handles are stored normalised to the segment (u = (V − Sj) ÷ (Sj+1 − Sj)), so reshaping the path does not disturb the timing; they are displayed in distance units.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: - Evaluation for fj ≤ f ≤ fj+1: compute V(f), clamp it to [Sj, Sj+1] (no travelling outside the segment), and take the path point at that arc length (§9.2). The curve may be non-monotonic (the node then moves back along the path).
source_units.note: Round-1 divergence closed by response implementation; see round-2 finding closure table.

source_units.text: - **Control-point passage frame:** the smallest f in [fj, fj+1] with V(f) ≥ the control point's arc length, found by bisection to 1e-4 frame and reported rounded to 3 decimals. Changing the velocity changes these frames.
source_units.note: Round-1 divergence closed by response implementation; see round-2 finding closure table.

source_units.text: - **Removing a motion keyframe** turns its pin into an ordinary intermediate velocity key (same frame, same normalised position in the merged segment), preserving the timing as far as possible.

source_units.text: 1. **Numeric equivalents for every gesture.** Every tool gesture of §5, §13.4 and §14 has a command equivalent taking numeric values: moving/rotating/scaling/skewing (`anim.transform.set`), motion-point editing (`anim.path.*`), handle editing in the function editor (`anim.function.key.set`), FOV wedge dragging (`anim.camera.set`), bone posing (`anim.bone.pose.set`, `anim.bone.reach.apply`), influence-zone editing (`anim.bone.influence.set`), ghost dragging (`anim.transform.set` with `target: "static"` and `relative: true` on the child), arms (rotation of the peg), and motion recording from a supplied sample list (`anim.record.run`). Interactive pointer simulation (section 11 `pointer`) remains available but is never required.
source_units.note: SI-097: skeleton transform only; bone kinematics excluded.

source_units.text: 2. **No modal paths.** The add-motion-point dialog maps to `anim.path.point.add` parameters; paste special maps to `anim.point.paste {properties}`; cut special maps to `anim.channel.cut {channels}`; confirmations do not exist in this area; warnings (e.g. `anim.pathEndConverted`) are returned in the result's `warnings` array and never block.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: 3. **Explicit targets.** Commands address nodes by id (or path, section 11) and never depend on the active tool, the view or peg-only mode. Commands that "act on the selection" in the GUI take an explicit `nodeIds` list; when it is omitted they use the current selection.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: 4. **Frames.** All `frame` parameters are **scene frames** (1-based integers; fractional only where stated). A frame inside a repeated loop cycle (not the first cycle) cannot be keyed (`anim.frameInvalid`). Omitted `frame` means the current frame.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: 5. **Read-back for verification.** `anim.evaluate` returns static, animated, local and world transforms, world bounds and output-pixel bounds of any node at any frames — agents verify placement without rendering. `anim.path.get`, `anim.path.sample`, `anim.function.get`, `anim.function.sample`, `anim.key.list`, `anim.skeleton.get`, `anim.skeleton.deform.get`, `anim.camera.get` and `anim.projection.get` expose every other model; `render_frame` (section 11) gives the visual check.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: 6. **Determinism.** Given the same document and commands, results are bit-for-bit reproducible across runs on the same platform and equal within 1e-6 across platforms (§2). Motion recording from samples does not depend on wall-clock time.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: 7. **Atomicity and undo.** Each action is one undo step; `batch` makes several one step. Invalid input changes nothing and returns an `anim.*` error with `{code, message, data}` where `data` carries limits or the conflicting frame/id.
source_units.note: Numeric/command implementation supported by the executed SDK matrix, independent maths/query probes, and c32_semantics/contract/readiness.

source_units.text: 8. **Events.** Changes are announced on `app://events` (§19.4) so agents can keep caches coherent.
